subject: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@acme.io>, Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window

Hi Sanjeev / Bethany,

Quick note after the sprint check — we are seeing two evaluation checkpoints slip by ~4 business days due to the longer-than-expected integration validation on ACME's staging. Given the downstream impact to the scheduled cutover, I propose we adopt a short containment MAP to preserve the original acceptance criteria while buying a small execution buffer.

Proposed immediate actions (low-regret):
- Freeze non-blocking feature changes for the eval run (effective immediately).
- Move up the rollback/fallback validation to June 13 so we have a canary window.
- Add a single contingency milestone: "Acceptance window +10 business days" with explicit sign-off criteria (attached checklist).
- Update the risk log entry for this MAP with owner and mitigation ETA.

Attached: MAP_v3.xlsx (proposed timeline + owner cells filled), risk_log_snapshot.pdf, eval-checklist-20280610.docx.

Can you confirm acceptance of a single +10 business day contingency and whether procurement needs a heads-up on the revised signature date? If you prefer a narrower change (e.g., +5 business days), tell us and we’ll update the MAP and procurement notice.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

From: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@acme.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear options.

We accept the concept of a single contingency milestone but need clarification on two items:
1) Will the +10 business day contingency change any billing or committed SLAs in the draft SOW?
2) What are the exact acceptance gates (we want to ensure compliance with our security sampling schedule).

On (1) procurement will push if anything looks like a change to the billing cadence; on (2) please send the explicit acceptance checklist items you referred to. If we can get the canary validation on June 13 as you suggest, that helps a lot.

Also, given this is an integration delay on our side, can we lock in a fallback model variant (quantized) for production in case we still see a late regression post-cutover? Would like a short note in the MAP about automatic fallback routing.

— Sanjeev
Sanjeev Rao
VP Engineering, ACME Platform
(sanjeev@acme.io)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@acme.io>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window

+1 to Rachel's plan. Quick technical clarifications:
- Fallback model variant: we have a tested quantized variant (q8) that is compatible with the evaluation harness; we can include automatic routing rules in the MAP and a 24-hour rollback window for safety.
- Acceptance gates (from attached checklist): integration smoke (automated tests green), end-to-end latency within threshold on staging (median < 120ms), and two sample security scans completed.

Operational asks:
- Laura, can you add a single procurement-facing line to the MAP that states: "Contingency milestone is for scheduling only; no change to fees or SLAs unless mutually agreed in writing."
- Rachel, if leadership needs to approve any credit or SLA exception we should request that today; I can draft the exec note.

On the fallback — we'll add an automated routing policy and a one-click rollback playbook entry.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. PM, Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@acme.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window

Thanks team — we can agree to a +10 business day contingency as long as procurement has advance notice. Our internal review board meets next Wednesday and they need the contract signature date reflected for budgeting. Two points:
1) Procurement asks that the MAP explicitly call out who is authorized to approve the contingency (we propose ACME's procurement lead + Redwood sales director).
2) If there is any change that effectively shortens our acceptance window (e.g., rollback forced earlier), we need a 48-hour notification window to the customer success team.

We prefer no changes to the fee schedule. If Redwood wants to offer customer credit in exchange for a faster cutover path, please state the size/terms. Procurement will not approve anything that changes cost assumptions without a separate amendment.

Regards,
Bethany
Bethany Cole
VP Product Operations, Orchid Health
(bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@orchidhealth.com>, Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@acme.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan update — containment for deadline drift in evaluation window

All — thanks for the quick alignment. Summary and next steps (we'll publish an updated MAP_v3.xlsx with these changes):
- Contingency: +10 business days to the final acceptance window; owner = ACME Integration Lead; approvers = ACME Procurement Lead + Redwood Sales Director (Rachel Kim).
- Procurement clause: explicit line stating no changes to fees/SLAs unless signed amendment — Laura will add that language.
- Acceptance gates: as listed by Jonas — automated tests green, latency threshold, 2 security scans.
- Fallback: q8 quantized variant + automatic routing policy + 24-hour rollback window.
- Notification: 48-hour notice if rollback shortens acceptance; CS team to be notified by ACME.

Requesting one action from Redwood leadership: if ACME requests any SLA credit for the delay (unlikely at this moment), request approval for a discretionary credit up to 10% of first-month fees for this deal (DL-8921). Jonas, Laura — can you confirm whether that needs exec sign-off or is within our delegated discount authority?

If no objections by EOD tomorrow (June 13), I'll upload the updated MAP and ping procurement + DocuSign links.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAP_v3.xlsx, risk_log_snapshot.pdf, eval-checklist-20280610.docx
